items.title: The comb-block decomposition criterion
items.strategy: Define the global hypothesis of Lemma 5.1 exactly: every sufficiently large comb block in every complement-family-free graph splits into an F1-free part and a pure blockade whose pattern is F2-free, with the stated cross-block vertexwise purity. Keep this criterion separate from property (*) so the later theorem has a visible hypothesis.

items.title: A large Y-part gives the first property (*) outcome
items.strategy: Apply an Erdős–Hajnal constant for F1 to an F1-free Y_i of size at least w/2, then use w >= 4 to compare (w/2)^c with w^(c/2).

items.title: Transversal large pure blocks give the third property (*) outcome
items.strategy: Choose one width-w/(2 ell) block from each decomposition. Use the cross-block condition in both directions to turn vertexwise purity into a pure pair, then use 2 ell <= ell^2 to obtain the third property (*) blockade.

items.title: Integral geometric layers of a size-ordered pure blockade
items.strategy: For ell >= 4 and t blocks in nonincreasing size order, define q = ceil(log_(sqrt ell) t) and integral cutoffs m_k = min(t, ceil(ell^(k/2))). The kth layer is the consecutive union from m_(k-1)+1 through m_k; these ceiling cutoffs repair the source's nonintegral indices.

items.title: Integral geometric layers force a blockade or a small union
items.strategy: In a size-ordered pure blockade with F2-free pattern, a layer with no block below w/ell^(5k/2) lifts an Erdős–Hajnal homogeneous set in the pattern to a complete or anticomplete blockade. If every such exit fails, choose one small block from each earlier layer and bound the next layer with the explicit ceiling-cutoff geometric tail, obtaining total size less than w/2.

items.title: The structural comb-decomposition criterion implies property (*)
items.strategy: Let c be the smaller of the two Erdős–Hajnal constants and take c_1 = c_3 = c/2 and c_2 = 5/c. Under failure of the three property (*) outcomes, the Y lemma makes every X_i at least w/2; the transversal lemma supplies one X_i with all blocks small; the integral-layer lemma then makes that X_i smaller than w/2, a contradiction.

title: The Structural Criterion for Property (*) — Examples

items.title: A four-tooth local comb-block decomposition
items.strategy: Give finite adjacency data for four teeth, their blocks, and a special vertex. Split each block into two pure subblocks with a P3-free two-vertex pattern and verify the three local clauses of the structural decomposition without claiming the universal criterion.

items.title: Integral geometric layers with a nonsquare base
items.strategy: Take ell = 5 and a size-ordered thirteen-block pure blockade. Compute q and every ceiling cutoff m_k, list the four integral layers, and check the resulting tail coefficients so the rounding repair is visible in a finite calculation.
